narrative: Material PL1__MFD3885C exhibits intermittent/lumpy demand with a CV of 1.34 and only 54.4% of working days showing non-zero consumption, indicating sporadic usage patterns. Lead times are extremely short (mean 0.25 days) but relatively volatile (CV 0.95), producing a modest sigma-over-lead-time of ~120 units. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 7,094 units and a data-driven safety stock of 197 units is recommended, replacing the significantly oversized SAP safety stock of 4,546 units. This policy maintains the 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory costs by approximately 69%.
warnings: SAP safety stock (4546) is 23x higher than the statistically optimal value (197); review ERP parameters.
Lead time CV of 0.95 indicates unstable supply; monitor supplier performance.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: The intermittent zero-inflated demand pattern and short but variable lead times are best served by a continuous-review (r,Q) policy, which triggers replenishment when stock falls to the reorder point r=279, ordering a fixed EOQ quantity Q=7,094. This balances the low unit holding cost against the fixed ordering cost and avoids over-ordering under lumpy demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap of 9,865.8 units constrains the unconstrained EOQ; however, the computed policy (197+7094=7291) is within capacity at 73.9% utilization. If safety stock were to be set at the SAP level of 4546, the remaining storage for an order would be only 5319 units, below the unconstrained EOQ — a capacity-binding situation that the optimized policy avoids.
